title: The Most Excited Employee in the Building
excerpt: The things that once filled us with excitement often become the ones we stop noticing. Sometimes nothing has changed – except our perspective.
body:
When I first started working at a veterinary hospital, I was probably the most excited person there, which was impressive considering my job involved cleaning kennels, folding towels, helping the groomers, and discovering that one wet dog can somehow soak an entire room.

I loved everything about the hospital. I loved my scrubs, my badge, the busy hallways, and the medical words I barely understood but fully intended to pretend I did. If a veterinarian asked me to help with something, I felt as though I had been personally selected for a highly classified mission.

At that point, even small things felt important. A new task made my day. Being trusted with something outside my usual duties felt like a promotion. I noticed everything because everything was new.

A few years later, the same hospital felt completely ordinary. The hallways were just hallways. The badge was something I forgot at home. The mysterious medical language had become background noise, and the excitement I once felt seemed to have disappeared.

For a while, I thought the job had changed. In reality, I had simply become used to it.

That happens in life more often than we realize. The home we once dreamed about becomes the place where the laundry lives. The relationship that once felt exciting becomes a discussion about groceries. Even the life we worked hard to build can quietly turn into something we barely notice.

Familiarity makes life easier, but it also has a talent for making good things invisible.

Sometimes we do not need a completely new life. We just need to remember what once made the old one feel special.

What made you ridiculously excited on your first day at work?
